title: App Definition
description: The single, versioned, validated contract that fully describes an application. The AI emits this document (never freeform code); the runtime, UI, and dev->prod promotion pipeline all consume it. Runtime-provided base fields (Id, CompanyId, AppId, CreatedAt/By, UpdatedAt/By, DeletedAt, RecordState) are implicit on every entity and MUST NOT be declared here — note the lifecycle base field is 'record_state' (active/archived), leaving the key 'status' free for a business field.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS App Definition schema the document targets.

key.description: Machine identifier for the app, unique within a company.

version.description: Semantic version of the app definition itself; bumped on every published change (drives dev->prod promotion).

archetype.description: What kind of app this fundamentally is — the recurring shape of the work, not the industry. The domain pass classifies it; the design pass builds the app's signature working surface from it instead of defaulting to generic CRUD screens.

kind.description: The primary archetype: tracker (system of record: registries, inventory, assets), pipeline (records advance through stages toward win/close: CRM, deals, recruiting), approval (request -> review -> approve/reject: expenses, leave, procurement), scheduling (people/resources placed on time slots: shifts, bookings, appointments), assignment (distributing people/items across stations/teams/owners), ticketing (intake queue triaged to resolution: helpdesk, incidents), planning (work broken into tasks/phases toward a date: projects, events, sprints), catalog (browse offerings and request them: service catalog, asset library), analytics (metrics/reporting are the product), forms (users design forms at runtime and collect responses).

coreJob.description: One concrete sentence naming the app's single core job and the working surface a user opens it to do that job (e.g. 'Assign employees to station shifts week by week on a board').

plugins.description: First-party or custom plugins this app enables.

visibleWhen.description: Show this block only when the condition holds — evaluated CLIENT-SIDE against the scope chain, so it can read screen state ('{{state.mode}}'), the bound record/row, or the actor. Give `value` (an expression) plus one of `eq`/`neq`/`in`. This is how a day/week toggle swaps which grid renders, or approval controls show only while pending. Exactly one of eq/neq/in — with none the block is always visible.

value.description: An expression resolved against the scope chain, e.g. '{{state.mode}}' or '{{record.status}}'.

eq.description: Show when the resolved value equals this.

neq.description: Show when the resolved value does not equal this.

in.description: Show when the resolved value is one of these.

fieldPath.description: A field key on the current row, or ONE hop through a reference field to a field on its target ('shift.start_time' = the start time of the shift this assignment points at). The hop is what lets a row be keyed or labelled by a fact it does not itself carry — an assignment knows its shift, but the DATE lives on the shift. Exactly one hop; the hop must land on a plain value, not on another reference.

filter.description: One condition. Address the value with EITHER 'field' (a key on the row) OR 'path' (one hop through a reference) — exactly one of the two.

path.description: Filter on a field one relation away — 'shift.shift_date' filters assignments by the date of their shift. Use this instead of 'field' when the fact you are filtering on lives on the referenced record.

value.description: A literal, or a SCOPE TOKEN resolved when the block renders: '{{actor.id}}' (the signed-in user — this is how a view becomes personal: 'my tickets', not everyone's), '{{today}}', '{{record.<field>}}' (the detail record), '{{item.<field>}}' (the nearest enclosing repeat row), '{{state.<key>}}' (the page's screen state, e.g. a filter-bar facet), or '{{<name>.<field>}}' for any repeat that declared `as: <name>`. A cell in a grid names BOTH axes at once: value '{{row.id}}' on one filter and '{{col.date}}' on another. Ranges: 'between' takes the inclusive pair [lo, hi]; 'overlaps' the window [from, to]; 'in'/'notIn' a list. Clock tokens work in any of those slots: '{{today}}', '{{now}}', '{{today+7}}', '{{today-2w}}', '{{now-4h}}' (units d/w/h; no month unit).

optional.description: When true, this leaf is SKIPPED whenever its resolved value is empty — so a page facet ('all owners') drops out of the filter set instead of matching only rows with a blank value. Pair with a '{{state.<key>}}' value that an unset facet leaves empty.

endField.description: For 'overlaps' only: the field holding the END of this row's range. The row's range is [field, endField]; the value is the window [from, to].
